variants.task: Create /tmp/eval_gemm/gemm.go (package main). Read one line from stdin: 'N seed' (1 <= N <= 2048, 1 <= seed < 2^31 - 1). Build the two N x N input matrices from the Lehmer generator x_0 = seed, x_t = (48271 * x_(t-1)) mod (2^31 - 1): A[i][k] = x_(i*N + k + 1) / (2^31 - 1) and B[k][j] = x_(N*N + k*N + j + 1) / (2^31 - 1) (0-based i, j, k; the division in IEEE double precision). Compute C = A * B in double precision. Output N lines; line i holds two numbers: S_i = sum over j of C[i][j]^2 and M_i = max over j of C[i][j], each printed with at least 12 significant digits (graded with a relative tolerance of 1e-9). Grading runs hidden seeds and sizes, including N = 2048, which must finish within 12 s of CPU time (user + system, summed over all threads; 20 s of wall time at most): a naive triple loop whose innermost multiply-accumulate strides down a column of B is cache-hostile and will exceed that limit. /tmp/eval_gemm/sample_input.txt and /tmp/eval_gemm/sample_output.txt are a worked sample (N = 4). Package main. Compile with `go build -o gemm gemm.go`.
